newsitem.title: USA: U.S. industry output up strongly in February.
newsitem.headline: U.S. industry output up strongly in February.

text.p: Strong manufacturing activity boosted the nation's industrial output during February, the Federal Reserve said on Friday in a report that showed no sign of developing production bottlenecks.

Total industrial production climbed 0.5 percent after a revised 0.1 percent drop in January, the strongest monthly pickup in output since a 0.8 percent jump last November. Yet the capacity use rate -- a potential measure of inflation pressures -- barely edged up to 83.3 percent from a revised 83.2 percent in January and remained below the 83.5 percent operating rate reached last December.
The pickup in February output of manufactured goods was broadly based.
"The increase resulted from gains in the production of durable consumer goods, business equipment , construction supplies and durable materials," the Fed said.

At the same time, exceptionally warm weather after a cold January led to a sharp drop in production of energy products as demand eased. That was also reflected in an earlier report on Friday from the Labour Department showing a sharp decline in prices for gasoline and home heating oil that helped shrink overall prices at the wholesale level by 0.4 percent last month.

Manufacturing output jumped 0.8 percent in February following a 0.2 percent drop in January. Mining industries pushed their production up by a sharp 1.3 percent after a 0.6 percent decline in January.

The only major industrial category in which output declined during February was utilities, down 3.5 percent following a 1.3 percent rise in January. That was likely related to reduced demand for electricty and other heating products because of the milder weather.
Analysts said the report was comforting from an inflation viewpoint.
"One can characterise the manufacturing sector as gradually showing improvement," said Cheryl Katz, an economist with Merrill Lynch Government Securities in New York.
"I believe there continue to be few bottlenecks at the manufacturing level, which is a good sign for inflation."
Federal Reserve policy-makers are scheduled to meet on March 25 to consider whether to raise interest rates for the first time in nearly two years.

The central bank commented earlier this week, in its Beige Book report on the national economy, that prices remain well-behaved despite the economy's steady growth. But it also noted that labour markets were tight across the country.

Carmakers edged up their production in February to a rate of 6.1 million new cars a year from 6.0 million in January but cut back assemblies of light trucks to 6.0 million from 6.1 million in January.
